title: Moody's Baa − Aaa Corporate Credit Spread
revision_note: FRED's H.15 monthly average of Moody's seasoned corporate bond yields is not revised after publication.

inputs.label: Moody's seasoned Aaa- and Baa-rated corporate bond yields, monthly averages (FRED AAA, BAA)

methodology: Baa − Aaa = FRED BAA − FRED AAA, computed per month in Python from Moody's own seasoned corporate bond yield indices (both covering maturities of twenty years and above), monthly averages, both starting 1919-01. A month is emitted only where both legs report — no forward-fill or interpolation.

This is a quality spread between two Moody's seasoned-bond yield indices, not an option-adjusted spread over a Treasury curve. Differencing two long-maturity corporate yields cancels out the term premium common to both, leaving (approximately) the credit-quality compensation the market demands for Baa-rated risk over Aaa-rated risk.
notes: Values are percentage points (1.25 means the Baa yield sits 1.25 points above the Aaa yield), not a decimal fraction.

AAA and BAA (monthly) both start 1919-01; do not confuse with FRED's DAAA/DBAA (daily), which start 1983 and 1986 respectively and would trade a century of clean monthly history for a cadence change — not used here.

Decided 2026-09-17: this chart was originally scoped on ICE BofA option-adjusted spreads (FRED BAMLC0A0CM investment-grade, BAMLH0A0HYM2 high-yield) and was rescoped onto the Moody's pair for two reasons. FRED now carries only a rolling three-year window of the ICE BofA series (all start 2023-09-18), which contains no recession and so defeats the point of showing risk appetite across cycles; and ICE Data Indices' terms are restricted, which would force this chart unpublished. The Moody's Baa/Aaa pair reaches back to 1919 instead, at the cost of being a narrower quality-only spread than the investment-grade/high-yield pair originally intended.

The spread has historically stayed positive (Baa, the lower credit quality, yields more than Aaa) but is not defined to be so by construction; a future observation crossing zero would be a real, reportable event, not a data error.

presentation.summary: Monthly Moody's Baa-minus-Aaa corporate bond yield spread, from FRED, back to 1919, with NBER recessions shaded.
